title: Fantasy Foosball Weekly: Year 8, Week 7 Preview
subtitle: With six playoff spots available, modeled odds frame six very different races.

playoffModel.description: Seeded Monte Carlo estimate using current record, scoring strength and remaining Sleeper schedule.

matchups.headline: A .500 matchup with sharply different playoff outlooks
matchups.paragraph: Payton’s I ♥️ Big Tet-Tees and Kade’s CheesusJesus both enter at 3-3, but their standings positions and modeled playoff chances tell different stories. Payton sits sixth with a 76.5% playoff chance, while Kade is seventh at 17.8%. A win would lift Payton to 85.2% and Kade to 32.8%; a loss would drop them to 58.5% and 10.6%, respectively. In this early-season race, those volatile swings make a closely matched record especially meaningful.

matchups.headline: Andy’s strong position meets Kohlt’s high-leverage opportunity
matchups.paragraph: Andy’s Long dong silvers are 5-1 and ranked second, carrying an 87% modeled playoff chance into a matchup with Kohlt’s 3-3, eighth-place kohlt. The model gives Andy a 94% chance with a win and 77.3% with a loss, so the favorite remains well positioned either way. Kohlt’s outlook is more volatile: a victory raises the modeled chance from 22.5% to 36%, while defeat lowers it to 12.6%. Six playoff spots keep this result consequential.

matchups.headline: Kane holds the safety net while Parker needs a pivot
matchups.paragraph: Kane’s Blueballs are 4-2 and ranked fifth, with a 96.8% modeled playoff chance before facing Parker’s 1-5, 11th-place My BallDak hurts. Kane’s odds move only from 96.8% to 98.7% with a win or 93.3% with a loss, making the matchup less urgent for the favorite. Parker’s modeled chance is 9.9%, rising to 18.1% with victory and falling to 5.5% in defeat. Parker’s 2019 title is part of the league lore, but the current model reflects a difficult position.

matchups.headline: Joey’s narrow path faces an already settled model
matchups.paragraph: Joey’s Off Constantly enters 2-4 in ninth place with a 1.6% modeled playoff chance, while Brae’s Ogles Outlaws are 0-6 and ranked 12th. The model gives Joey a small increase to 2.4% with a win and a drop to 0.4% with a loss, a two-point swing that underscores how limited the path is. Brae’s playoff chance remains 0% regardless of the result. Joey, the 2024 champion, therefore faces a long-shot opportunity rather than a broad shift in the standings picture.

matchups.headline: First place has room to breathe against a former champion
matchups.paragraph: Evan’s Bonnie Blue 42 sit atop the standings at 5-1, with a 99.7% modeled playoff chance before meeting Cooper’s 2-4, 10th-place Jack MeHoff. Evan’s odds barely move: they reach 99.9% with a win and remain 98.8% with a loss. Cooper’s already slim 0.2% chance rises to 1% with victory and falls to 0.1% in defeat. The matchup pairs the league leader, a 2023 champion, with Cooper’s 2022 championship history.

matchups.headline: A ranked 4-2 duel with nearly identical playoff footing
matchups.paragraph: Alex’s I love big TD’s and CJ’s cjbroadway23 are both 4-2, with Alex ranked fourth and CJ third. Their modeled playoff chances are similarly strong: 94.6% for Alex and 93.4% for CJ, fitting a matchup where the stakes are real but neither team is in immediate danger. Alex rises to 98% with a win and drops to 91.3% with a loss; CJ moves to 97.6% or 89.1%. Alex, the 2025 champion, brings recent league history to a tightly balanced contest.
